problem.title: Across a Tiny Grid
problem.statement: A marker starts at the lower-left point of a grid and must reach the upper-right point using exactly 2 moves right and 2 moves up, in any order. How many shortest paths are possible?
hints: Separate paths by whether their final move is right or up.
Alternatively, choose the two positions occupied by the up moves.

solutionSteps.title: Fix the moves
solutionSteps.body: Every shortest path contains two R moves and two U moves.

solutionSteps.title: Choose the U positions
solutionSteps.body: Choose 2 of the 4 step positions for U; the other two positions are R.

solutionSteps.title: Count paths
solutionSteps.body: There are C(4,2) = 6 possible move strings.

validationMethods: independent enumeration of RRUU, RURU, RUUR, URRU, URUR, UURR
notes: The nine-point distractor diagnoses counting grid points instead of paths.

problem.title: Robot Route
problem.statement: A robot must travel from one grid point to another using exactly 3 moves right and 2 moves up. If it never moves left or down, how many shortest routes can it take?
hints: There are five step positions in total.
Choose the two positions for the up moves.

solutionSteps.title: Encode a route
solutionSteps.body: Every shortest route is a five-character string with three R symbols and two U symbols.

solutionSteps.title: Choose positions
solutionSteps.body: Choose 2 of 5 positions for U; the remaining positions are R.

solutionSteps.title: Count
solutionSteps.body: C(5,2)=10 routes.

notes: Both path encodings count each 3R-2U string once.

problem.title: Park Walk
problem.statement: A walker takes a shortest grid route consisting of exactly 4 blocks east and 2 blocks north. How many different shortest routes are there?
hints: A shortest route has six moves.
Choose the positions of the two north moves.

solutionSteps.title: Fix the inventory
solutionSteps.body: Every shortest route contains four E moves and two N moves.

solutionSteps.title: Choose north positions
solutionSteps.body: Choose 2 of the 6 positions for N.

validationMethods: independent recurrence rows 1,5,15 for zero, one, and two north moves

problem.title: Drone on a Street Grid
problem.statement: A drone follows a shortest grid route with exactly 3 moves east and 3 moves north. How many move sequences are possible?
hints: There are six step positions.
Choose three positions for either direction.

solutionSteps.title: Encode
solutionSteps.body: A route is a six-position string with three E symbols and three N symbols.

solutionSteps.title: Choose
solutionSteps.body: Choose 3 of 6 positions for N.

problem.title: Library Cart
problem.statement: A library cart follows a shortest route made of exactly 5 moves right and 2 moves up. How many shortest move sequences are possible?
hints: The route has seven moves.
Choose the two positions for U.

solutionSteps.title: Fix seven positions
solutionSteps.body: Every route uses five R moves and two U moves.

solutionSteps.title: Choose up positions
solutionSteps.body: The U symbols can occupy any 2 of 7 positions.

validationMethods: independent sum 1+2+3+4+5+6=21 by the location of the second up move

problem.title: Closed Intersection
problem.statement: A courier travels from (0,0) to (3,2), moving only one unit right or one unit up. The intersection (1,1) is closed and cannot be visited. How many shortest routes remain?
hints: Give the closed point a path count of zero.
Or subtract paths through (1,1) from all C(5,2) unrestricted paths.

solutionSteps.title: Count all routes
solutionSteps.body: Without the closure there are C(5,2)=10 routes.

solutionSteps.title: Count routes through the closure
solutionSteps.body: There are C(2,1)=2 ways to reach (1,1) and C(3,1)=3 ways to continue, giving 6 forbidden routes.

solutionSteps.title: Remove forbidden routes
solutionSteps.body: 10−6=4 legal routes remain.

notes: The two methods independently confirm that six unrestricted paths are invalid.

problem.title: Route Through a Checkpoint
problem.statement: A robot moves from (0,0) to (4,3), one unit right or up at a time, and must pass through (2,1). How many shortest routes satisfy the requirement?
hints: Split the route at the required point.
Count routes into and out of the checkpoint separately.

solutionSteps.title: Reach the checkpoint
solutionSteps.body: From (0,0) to (2,1), choose the one U position among three: C(3,1)=3.

solutionSteps.title: Leave the checkpoint
solutionSteps.body: From (2,1) to (4,3), choose two U positions among four: C(4,2)=6.

solutionSteps.title: Join the stages
solutionSteps.body: Each incoming route can continue along each outgoing route, so 3×6=18.

validationMethods: independent enumeration by the checkpoint arrival string and four-step departure count

problem.title: First Move East
problem.statement: A shortest grid route uses exactly 5 east moves and 3 north moves. How many such routes begin with an east move?
hints: Fix the required first move before counting.
Seven positions remain for four E and three N moves.

solutionSteps.title: Fix the first step
solutionSteps.body: Place E in the first position, using one of the five east moves.

solutionSteps.title: Arrange what remains
solutionSteps.body: The remaining seven positions contain four E symbols and three N symbols.

solutionSteps.title: Count
solutionSteps.body: Choose the three N positions: C(7,3)=35.

validationMethods: independent ratio check: 5/8 of C(8,3)=56 gives 35

problem.title: Diagonal Step Strings
problem.statement: A marker makes 6 diagonal upward steps. Each step goes one column left or one column right. To finish 2 columns to the right of where it started, how many left-right step strings are possible if there are no board edges?
hints: Let r and l be the numbers of right and left steps.
Solve r+l=6 and r−l=2, then choose positions.

solutionSteps.title: Find the move inventory
solutionSteps.body: The equations r+l=6 and r−l=2 give r=4 and l=2.

solutionSteps.title: Choose positions
solutionSteps.body: Choose the 2 left-step positions among the 6 total steps.

validationMethods: solve r+l=6 and r−l=2 then calculate C(6,2)=15
independent Pascal recurrence for six unrestricted left-right steps at displacement two

problem.title: Two Closed Intersections
problem.statement: A courier moves from (0,0) to (4,4), one unit right or up at a time. The intersections (1,2) and (3,2) are closed. How many shortest routes avoid both intersections?
hints: Write zero at both closed points.
Fill each remaining point by adding its left and lower predecessor counts.

solutionSteps.title: Seed the grid
solutionSteps.body: Write 1 at (0,0) and 0 at each closed point.

solutionSteps.title: Propagate legal counts
solutionSteps.body: At every other point, add the legal counts immediately left and below.

solutionSteps.title: Read the destination
solutionSteps.body: The two destination predecessors contain 10 and 9 paths, giving 19.

validationMethods: cross-check 70−30−30+9=19 by correcting overlap among routes through the two closed points
notes: The learner-facing primary method uses only C10 recurrence; the second method independently verifies the answer.

problem.title: Two Required Checkpoints
problem.statement: A robot moves from (0,0) to (5,4), one unit right or up at a time, and must visit (1,1) and then (3,3). How many shortest routes satisfy both requirements?
hints: Split the route into three sections at the two checkpoints.
Multiply because every choice for one section can join every choice for the next.

solutionSteps.title: First section
solutionSteps.body: From (0,0) to (1,1), there are C(2,1)=2 routes.

solutionSteps.title: Middle section
solutionSteps.body: From (1,1) to (3,3), there are C(4,2)=6 routes.

solutionSteps.title: Final section
solutionSteps.body: From (3,3) to (5,4), there are C(3,1)=3 routes.

solutionSteps.title: Join sections
solutionSteps.body: Multiply the independent section choices: 2×6×3=36.

validationMethods: independent nested enumeration of 2 first-section choices, 6 middle strings, and 3 final strings
